scripture.text:
For there is no good tree which produces bad fruit, nor, on the other hand, a bad tree which produces good fruit. For each tree is known by its own fruit. For men do not gather figs from thorns, nor do they pick grapes from a briar bush. The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth what is good; and the evil man out of the evil treasure brings forth what is evil; for his mouth speaks from that which fills his heart.
“Why do you call Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I say? Everyone who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them, I will show you whom he is like:

exposition.text: Luke 6:43-47 opens with a scene marked by faithful response to God's word. The text does not ask the reader to admire the moment from a distance. The passage puts one clear scene in front of us: Everyone who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them. We should stay with that scene before we rush to a slogan. Because this is narrative material, the theology arrives through events, actions, and speech rather than detached maxims. That keeps the reading honest. The wider context matters too. Luke 6:43-47 belongs to a larger movement in which Jesus is being received, resisted, watched, and answered. So the burden here is faithful response to God's word. The theological lane is faithful response to God's word. The passage stays concrete through For there is no good tree which and everyone, who, comes. What we see in Luke 6:43-47 shows how people respond when Jesus stands near and the cost of discipleship is no longer theoretical. The point is not bare information. It presses into faithful response instead of vague admiration. We should not drift into generic encouragement detached from the scene. We should let the passage name the pressure point for the day. If the scene is shaped by Everyone who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them, then obedience today should answer that same pressure point. Where the text exposes fear, we should answer the word with concrete obedience. Where it honors devotion, we should practice concrete obedience under the authority of the passage. Where it reveals Jesus clearly, we should pursue steady trust in the ordinary places of life rather than delay. That keeps the day under the authority of Scripture. Strong exposition stays close to the text. It does not chase a clever slogan. It lets the details do their work on the conscience. That kind of reading slows us down. It teaches us to listen before we react. It also keeps prayer and application from drifting away from the passage. The passage sustains courage because Jesus remains worthy of trust in costly moments. The church's witness is strengthened when daily conduct aligns with confessed doctrine. The text rewards slow attention because its details are part of its theology, not background decoration. Good application therefore grows from disciplined reading rather than from devotional instinct alone. prompts: Sit with Luke 6:43-47 for two quiet minutes. Read the scene of faithful response to God's word slowly and let it settle before you move on.
Where does this passage call for concrete obedience under the authority of the passage today?
Stay for one more minute and answer God with one honest sentence of trust, repentance, or gratitude before continuing.

items: Speak one truthful and encouraging sentence to someone today as a direct response to Luke 6:43-47.
Set aside ten minutes to practice the obedience this reflection emphasized instead of postponing it.

prayer.text: Father, thank You for speaking clearly in Luke 6:43-47. In this passage You bring faithful response to God's word into the open through Everyone who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them. Lord Jesus, keep us from reading these words as distant history only, and press them into our ordinary obedience today. Where we resist the truth highlighted in this reflection, bring repentance and renewed trust. Keep us near Your word, and do not let ordinary pressure turn us away from humble obedience. Holy Spirit, take what we have seen in the exposition and turn it into worship instead of mere information. Teach us to remember that Luke 6:43-47 opens with a scene marked by faithful response to God's word. Guard our speech from haste, our work from pride, and our choices from whatever would pull us away from faithful response instead of vague admiration. Help us practice the obedience this day requires with humility as we pursue concrete obedience under the authority of the passage. Amen.
